media_strategy.selection_principle: data-driven — the dataset is YouTube clips, so the multimodal centerpiece is real Super Bowl ad embeds (free, hosted), supplemented by 2 atmospheric generated stills and a chart-led narrative. Asset budget: 2 generated images + 4 YouTube embeds (no audio/video generation due to disk constraint).

chart.reason: The dataset's centerpiece is the seven-trait coding across 244 ads; charts are the natural way to read trait shares, brand fingerprints, year-by-year drift, and trait correlations.

image.reason: Two atmospheric editorial stills (teaser, patriotic-spike chapter break) provide visual rhythm in an otherwise chart-led piece. The dataset is about the visual culture of Super Bowl ads, so a non-data still belongs.

video.reason: The dataset IS YouTube videos — every ad has a verified watch URL. We embed real Super Bowl ads (Doritos Sling Baby and Budweiser Born The Hard Way) directly rather than generating motion. This is the most data-faithful possible video strategy.

audio.reason: media_blocker — disk-budget cap of 5 generated assets. Two image generations are already used. Generated music or a sonification would exceed the cap, and a click-to-play tone card has been over-used in recent blogs. The Super Bowl ads dataset already supplies its own audio via the embedded YouTube clips (each clip has its own ad-jingle/voiceover audio bound to the visual).

interactive_or_map.reason: Reader-quiz interaction at edt_05 (the patriotic-spike reframing): readers guess which year was the patriotic peak before the chart reveals it was 2017, not 2002.

media_blockers.reason: Generated audio would exceed the run's 5-asset cap and tight disk budget. The piece's audio dimension is satisfied by the embedded YouTube ads which carry their original audio.
media_blockers.fallback_des: no audio item; visual fallback is the embedded ads themselves

des_01.label: Teaser hero — lonely glowing TV in a snack-strewn living room

content.prompt: Editorial cinematic still: a lone old-style cathode-ray television set glowing softly in a dark living room at night, the screen a soft amber color with no visible content, faint reflection on a coffee table littered with glossy snack-food wrappers and crumpled beer cans, warm tungsten light spilling from a lamp at the edge, subtle film grain, high contrast moody lighting, photographic, no text, no logos, 16:9 aspect ratio

des_01.brief: Full-bleed teaser image: a single warmly-lit CRT television in a dark room surrounded by Super Bowl detritus (chip bags, beer cans). The TV screen is intentionally blank/amber so the headline can sit over it. Mood: voyeuristic, intimate, nostalgic — the genuine viewing posture of the Super Bowl ad audience.
des_01.rationale: The blog argues the Super Bowl ad is a 30-second polygraph for the country. The teaser shows the testing chamber: a lit-up screen in a dark room with the audience already gone for the night. Withholds the data so the reader is curious.

des_02.label: Headline + subheadline stat callout

content.label: YouTube views — for one Doritos ad about a baby in a slingshot. 4,262 times the median ad in the dataset.

des_02.brief: Big bold number (54-72px), aligned center, with a subdued caption beneath. The number itself is the hook.
des_02.rationale: The first finding the reader meets needs to land hard. The 176M number is jaw-dropping enough on its own; we use a stat callout, not a chart.

des_03.label: Doritos 'Sling Baby' YouTube embed (the most-viewed ad)

content.caption: Doritos 'Sling Baby' (2012). 176 million views — the most-watched ad in the dataset, and a Crash the Super Bowl crowdsourced winner.

des_03.brief: Standard 16:9 YouTube iframe at full content width (720px). Caption beneath in muted serif. This is the literal punchline of the hook.
des_03.rationale: The hook claims a baby-in-a-slingshot is the most-watched Super Bowl ad of the era. Show, don't tell. Embed the actual clip.

des_04.label: Trait prevalence — bar chart of all 7 traits

content.interaction: hover tooltip showing exact count and percentage. Bars sorted by pct descending so funny is at top, patriotic at bottom.

style.palette: single accent (warm amber #d97706 like the teaser TV) on dark muted neutral
style.label_inside_bar: show pct label at end of bar

des_04.brief: Horizontal bar chart, 7 bars sorted from longest (funny 68.9%) to shortest (patriotic 16.8%). Single accent color matches the teaser amber. Number labels at the end of each bar. The patriotic bar gets a subtle outline/highlight to flag it as the rarest.
des_04.rationale: Seven categories on one comparison axis is the canonical bar-chart job. Sorted bars make the funny-dominance and patriotic-rarity instantly readable.

des_05.label: Trait stacking distribution — area or stat

content.label: average traits per ad (out of 7). Only 4 ads in 21 years check zero boxes; only 2 check six or seven.

des_05.brief: Compact stat showing the mean trait count. Small enough not to compete with the bar chart above.
des_05.rationale: The 'recipe is small handful, not single ingredient' point doesn't need its own chart — a stat callout is sufficient and keeps section pacing tight.

des_06.label: Brand fingerprint — small-multiples bar chart per brand

highlight.NFL: 0% bars (danger, animals, use_sex) get muted/zero indicator

content.interaction: hover tooltip showing brand + trait + exact pct

style.palette: single accent + neutral grey for non-highlight

des_06.brief: Ten small charts, two rows of five, one per brand. Each shows seven mini-bars (one per trait), sharing the same y-axis 0-100%. Brand name is the panel title. The shape of each panel IS the brand fingerprint — Bud Light's funny+fast spike, NFL's three flat zeros, Coca-Cola's animals tilt — readable at a glance.
des_06.rationale: Radar charts are showy but hard to compare side-by-side; a 5x2 grid of mini-bar charts uses the chart real estate efficiently and lets readers spot the unique 'shape' of each brand.

des_07.label: 21-year drift — multi-line trend chart of all 7 traits

content.interaction: hover any line for tooltip with year + trait + pct. Click trait legend to isolate that trait.

style.palette: warm-cool divergent — funny/use_sex/danger in warm tones (declining), patriotic/celebrity/animals in cool tones (rising)

des_07.brief: A 7-line trend chart from 2000 to 2020. Warm-toned lines (funny, use_sex, danger) trend down; cool-toned lines (patriotic, celebrity, animals) trend up. 2017 has dotted vertical guides showing where funny crashed and patriotic peaked. Legend is interactive — clicking a trait emphasizes it.
des_07.rationale: Time series across all 7 traits on one chart is dense, but it is the picture. Color-grouping by direction (warm = falling, cool = rising) does most of the cognitive work. Interactive legend prevents overload.

des_08.label: Era diff bar — 2000-2009 vs 2010-2020 change in pp

content.interaction: hover for tooltip showing both era percentages and the diff

style.palette: diverging red (negative pp) to green (positive pp)
style.sort: by change_pp ascending so funny is at bottom

des_08.brief: Diverging horizontal bars centered on a zero line. Negative bars (funny -27.4 pp, use_sex -13.8 pp, danger -8.0 pp) extend left in red. Positive bars (patriotic +12.7, celebrity +8.2, animals +5.8) extend right in green. The +/- 27 pp span makes the magnitude visceral.
des_08.rationale: The era comparison is the second-best summary of the whole story; a diverging bar visualizes 'which way did each trait move' in one glance.

des_09.label: Reader quiz — guess the patriotic peak year

content.initial_state: Reader sees the prompt 'Which year had the highest share of patriotic Super Bowl ads?' and 5 buttons: 2002, 2008, 2014, 2017, 2020. The chart of patriotic% by year is hidden (greyed out / blurred).
content.trigger: Reader clicks one of the 5 year buttons.
content.transition: Selected button highlights. The chart un-blurs. The selected year's bar gets a faint outline. The 2017 bar is accented with a label '60%'. A line above the chart says either 'Right!' (if 2017) or 'Most readers guess 2002 — the post-9/11 reflex. The data says 2017 (60%, the highest of any year).'
content.payoff: The chart reveals the full year-by-year patriotic% trajectory — flat through the 2000s, climbing through the 2010s, peaking in 2017.

des_09.brief: A guess-first interaction. Users commit to a year before seeing the chart, which makes the surprise of 2017 (vs. the obvious 2002 reflex) hit harder. After the reveal, the bar chart of patriotic% by year is fully visible and labeled.
des_09.rationale: The 9/11 vs 2017 reframing is the most counter-intuitive claim in the piece. A passive chart wouldn't deliver the surprise; a guess-first interaction does.

des_10.label: Patriotic chapter image — flag draped over empty stadium seats

content.prompt: Editorial photograph: a single American flag rendered in the shape of a Super Bowl ring or stadium-sized banner, draped softly over a row of empty stadium seats lit only by the spill of distant floodlights, deep blue cinematic shadows, warm sodium-vapor highlights on the fabric, no people, slight haze in the air, patriotic but melancholy mood, no text, no logos, no faces, 16:9

des_10.brief: Full-width chapter image used as a visual breakpoint between the surprise reveal (2017 spike) and the embedded Budweiser ad. Mood is contemplative, not jingoistic — empty seats, draped flag, cinematic blue/orange.
des_10.rationale: After the quiz reveals the 2017 spike, the reader needs a beat to absorb. A still image gives that pause without filling it with another chart.

des_11.label: Budweiser 'Born The Hard Way' YouTube embed

content.caption: Budweiser, 'Born The Hard Way' (2017). 28.8 million views — the highest-viewed patriotic ad in the dataset. Tells the immigration story of Adolphus Busch, the brand's German founder.

des_11.brief: Embedded 16:9 YouTube iframe of the actual ad that defines the 2017 patriotic peak. Caption explains the immigration angle.
des_11.rationale: The 60% finding becomes textured when the reader can watch the specific spot that defined the peak — and notice that 'patriotic' here is also pro-immigration.

des_12.label: Trait correlation matrix heatmap

content.interaction: hover any cell for tooltip showing trait pair and phi coefficient

style.palette: diverging blue (negative) to red (positive) centered on white at zero

des_12.brief: 7x7 heatmap of pairwise trait correlations. The diagonal is muted (self=1.0 not informative). The funny-vs-patriotic cell is darkest blue at -0.384; funny-vs-danger and funny-vs-use_sex are darkest red at +0.275. Color legend below.
des_12.rationale: 21 trait pairs is too many for separate charts; a small heatmap is the standard form. The diverging color makes 'comedy and flag don't share a slot' visible at a glance.

des_13.label: Bud Light 'Save Yourself' bear-attack YouTube embed

content.caption: Bud Light, 'Save Yourself' (2006). The canonical Bud Light formula in 30 seconds: funny + animal + danger, no celebrity, no flag.

des_13.brief: Embed under the Bud Light/Doritos paragraph in edt_03. A live demonstration of the 'every Bud Light spot is funny' finding.
des_13.rationale: Brand-fingerprint chart says Bud Light is 95% funny + 35% animals + 45% danger. This 30-second clip shows what that recipe looks like cooked together.

des_14.label: Trait recipe ranking — top 10 most-common combinations

content.interaction: hover for tooltip showing exact count

des_14.brief: Horizontal bar chart of the top 10 trait recipes by ad count. The bare 'funny + show_product_quickly' pair tops the list at 23 ads. Caption notes that these ten recipes account for ~45% of all 244 ads.
des_14.rationale: The closing argument is that the genre runs on a small number of repeated recipes. Showing the actual top recipes is more concrete than a paragraph claim.

page_rhythm.tone: dark editorial — the teaser TV's amber against deep neutral, with patriotic blue/red as accents in section 5 only
page_rhythm.text_visual_pattern: alternating: every 2-3 paragraphs alternate with a chart, embed, or stat callout. Two YouTube embeds anchor the start (edt_01) and the surprise reveal (edt_05).
page_rhythm.centrepiece: des_07 (the 21-year multi-line drift chart) — visually the most information-dense piece, and the structural backbone of the article's claim.
page_rhythm.anti_sameness_notes: Avoids the Bud Light / Doritos-only narrative; centers the data, not the brands. Avoids the typical 'play this audio clip' card. Avoids fake patriotism — the patriotic image is melancholy, not triumphal.
page_rhythm.typography_notes: Big stat callout for 176M views uses tabular numerals at 60-72px. Section labels use small-caps. Pull-quote-style emphasis on the '60% — 2017' reveal. Body in serif (Georgia or Iowan Old Style), labels in system-ui.
